A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it scrambled, so people in between can't read it.

Here is the flow:

Your device locks your traffic and sends it to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unlocks it and visits the website for you.
The website sees the VPN's location, not yours.

Your Wi-Fi owner or internet provider only sees scrambled data going to the VPN. It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your location. It doesn't make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
